**My pick is the Baseus EnerFill FC41 (25,000 mAh) if you want to charge a laptop and a phone. If you only need to top up a phone, get the Baseus PicoGo AM52.**

## Top picks
- **Best all-around: [Baseus EnerFill FC41, 25,000 mAh, 145 W](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-enerfill-fc41-25000mah-145w)**, $79.99. The code FC41 reportedly brings it to $67.99. It's about 91 Wh, under the 100 Wh limit, with two built-in USB-C cables and up to 140 W from one port, enough for a laptop. The listing doesn't publish its weight.
- **Slim laptop option: [Baseus Blade H1, 20,000 mAh, 100 W](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah)**, $89.99. At about 74 Wh and 18 mm thick, it's easy to pack, and it weighs about 451 g.
- **Lightest, phone only: [Baseus PicoGo AM52, 10,000 mAh Qi2.2 magnetic](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w)**, $59.99. The code AM52 reportedly brings it to $53.99. It's about 37 Wh, but at 45 W it won't charge a laptop well.

These links are affiliate links from Dealectric, the source I'm drawing on, and the site earns a commission. It also lists other brands (Anker, UGREEN, INIU and more) in a comparison table, including a cheaper laptop-capable INIU at $46.99: [Dealectric's full comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-power-banks-for-flying). I haven't verified the prices or discount codes myself.

## Rules to know
- **Carry-on only:** the [FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7) says power banks can't go in checked bags. If your carry-on gets gate-checked, take the power bank out first.
- **Size limit:** the FAA allows up to 100 Wh per battery. Watt-hours = mAh × 3.7 ÷ 1,000, so 25,000 mAh is about 92.5 Wh. Anything over 100 Wh needs airline approval, and over 160 Wh is banned ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)).
- **Airlines can be stricter:** [Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters) allows only one power bank per customer (since April 20, 2026). It must stay out of the overhead bin, be visible while in use, and not be charged from seat power. Per Dealectric's table, American and Delta allow two at 100 Wh each with no recharging on board, and JetBlue allows two with no charging from seat power. Check your airline before you fly.
- **Recalls:** don't bring a recalled or damaged bank. Anker recalled several models in June 2025, listed in the Dealectric article.

Since Southwest allows only one bank and wants it visible, a single 25,000 mAh unit like the FC41 works well across airlines.
